newsitem.title: CHINA: China boosts minimum wage in many areas.
newsitem.headline: China boosts minimum wage in many areas.

text.p: Chinese provincial and municipal governments are raising their minimum wage levels to keep pace with inflation, the China Daily said on Thursday.
The new minimum wage level is designed to guarantee reasonable standards of living for employees as competition for jobs intensifies and wage gaps widen, it said.

It said 12 of China's 30 provinces and municipalities had fixed new wage floors, ranging from a high of 398 yuan ($48) a month in the boomtown of Shenzhen near Hong Kong to 140 yuan in the less developed inland provinces of Guizhou and Gansu.
In Shenzhen the minimum wage had increased 4.7 percent compared with last year while Shanghai had raised its floor 11.1 percent to 300 yuan from last year's 270 yuan, it said.
The capital, Beijing, has set its new minimum at 270 yuan, up from 240 yuan last year.
Officials have estimated inflation will rise by less than 6.5 percent this year.

The minimum wage should be readjusted every year in accordance with inflation and should be less than the local average wage scale and more than social insurance or unemployment payouts, the newspaper quoted Li Xinwang, an official with the Comprehensive Plan and Wages Department under the Ministry of Labour, as saying. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
